title: Equalize policy kinetics
frozenQuestion: Does label-blind equalization of policy activation opportunity, experienced displacement, executed target range, and successful-action rate reduce composition-corrected aggregation after dynamic global and mobility-matched null correction?

scope.calibrationAnchors: balanced 50/50 pairwise, absent policy-value association, both input profiles
scope.progressDefinition: floor(progress * final accepted swaps), progress 0.00 through 1.00; censored runs retain their observed event-budget trajectory
scope.metric: paper-denominator same-policy adjacency minus the validated S02 exact-composition expectation

labelBlindBoundary.policyPreservation: The native policy function, direction, observations, comparisons, target, and Selection cursor update are unchanged. An intervention may choose the next actor through a state-blind scheduler or reject an otherwise mechanically valid native swap; it may not rewrite a proposal or target.
labelBlindBoundary.audit: Repeat representative runs after assigning arbitrary secret analysis labels; every transition, kinetic ledger, trajectory, and terminal result must be identical. Source-level tests forbid analysis_label access in the intervention module.

kineticDefinitions.activationOpportunity: actor activations per cell, normalized by total activations / n; policy value 1 denotes equal per-cell opportunity
kineticDefinitions.experiencedDisplacement: sum of absolute positional displacement over both identities moved by each accepted swap, attributed to each displaced identity's executable policy, divided by policy cell count and by total activations / 10000
kineticDefinitions.actorDisplacement: sum of absolute native actor-to-target distance for accepted swaps initiated by a policy, divided by its actor activations
kineticDefinitions.executedTargetRange: mean absolute actor-to-target distance among accepted native swap proposals initiated by the policy
kineticDefinitions.nativeTargetRange: mean absolute actor-to-target distance among all mechanically valid native swap proposals before intervention rejection
kineticDefinitions.successfulActionRate: accepted native swap proposals initiated by the policy divided by that policy's actor activations
kineticDefinitions.structuralIdentity: actor displacement per activation equals successful-action rate times executed target range whenever at least one accepted swap is present

regimes.scheduler: frozen E01 uniform counter-addressed actor scheduler
deterministic counter-addressed identity cycles; every cycle is a policy-blind permutation of all identities

regimes.swapGate: policy-indexed Bernoulli gate on mechanically valid native swaps, independent of target distance
distance gate exp(-kappa_policy * (distance - 1)) on mechanically valid native swaps; proposals and targets are unchanged
policy-indexed Bernoulli gate on mechanically valid native swaps, independent of target distance
policy-indexed Bernoulli gate multiplied by exp(-kappa_policy * (distance - 1))

calibration.holdoutIsolation: No holdout trajectory or endpoint may be read before all regime parameters and feasibility labels are frozen in calibration_models.json.
calibration.commonTarget: For displacement, target range, and success, use the minimum finite native calibration mean across policies so interventions only remove or defer native actions.
calibration.probabilityInitialization: For displacement_equal and success_equal, initialize each policy gate as min(1, common_target / native_policy_mean), clipped below at 0.02.
calibration.probabilityRefinement: At most two deterministic multiplicative updates using common_target / observed_policy_mean, clipped to [0.02, 1]. Retain the first feasible iterate; otherwise retain the lowest frozen objective.
calibration.targetRangeSelection: Choose the smallest kappa giving a feasible target-range regime. If none is feasible, choose the feasible candidate with the smallest target-range imbalance; if none preserves completion, retain the smallest-imbalance candidate and label it infeasible.
calibration.jointInitialization: Use identity-cycle activation plus the success-rate gate probabilities and selected target-range kappa; apply at most two deterministic probability refinements against displacement and success targets.
calibration.objective: mean squared normalized balance gap across the regime's named targets plus 100 times completion deficit and 25 times completion-comparability deficit

balanceAndFeasibility.activationTolerance: median pairwise absolute gap <= 0.02 and 90th percentile <= 0.04 in normalized per-cell activation opportunity
balanceAndFeasibility.displacementTolerance: median pairwise relative gap <= 0.10 and 90th percentile <= 0.20
balanceAndFeasibility.targetRangeTolerance: median pairwise absolute gap <= 0.25 positions and 90th percentile <= 0.50 positions
balanceAndFeasibility.successRateTolerance: median pairwise relative gap <= 0.10 and 90th percentile <= 0.20
balanceAndFeasibility.completionTolerance: at least 95% complete in every calibration anchor and no anchor more than 5 percentage points below paired native control
balanceAndFeasibility.regimeFeasible: all named balance targets and completion tolerance pass on calibration
balanceAndFeasibility.holdoutGeneralization: report the same gates without retuning; a calibration-feasible regime is not relabeled using holdout outcomes

nullsAndEndpoints.excludedDecisionOutcome: duration above zero; retained only as an explicitly non-discriminating descriptive field if emitted
nullsAndEndpoints.peak: maximum of the complete 101-point condition-mean corrected trajectory
nullsAndEndpoints.positiveArea: integral of the positive part of the piecewise-linear corrected trajectory
nullsAndEndpoints.adjustedEffect: observed endpoint minus mean of 500 complete-trajectory null endpoints
nullsAndEndpoints.effectInterval: observed endpoint minus the 97.5th and 2.5th null percentiles
nullsAndEndpoints.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg across 186 conditions separately within regime, null family, and outcome; intervention-versus-control contrasts use paired bootstrap intervals with familywise Bonferroni coverage over the six primary anchors
nullsAndEndpoints.valueConditioningBoundary: Value-stratified nulls are mechanism-sensitive diagnostics and never replace the global and mobility-matched primary endpoints.

primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.population: six balanced 50/50 pairwise absent-association holdout conditions
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.substantialReduction: for a calibration-feasible joint_equal regime, median paired reduction versus native control is at least 25% for both global-null adjusted peak and global-null adjusted positive area, and at least 4 of 6 Bonferroni intervals exclude zero in the reduction direction
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.mobilityRobustness: the direction of the median reduction is the same under mobility-matched null adjustment for peak and positive area
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.supportive: joint_equal is calibration-feasible and both substantialReduction and mobilityRobustness pass
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.null: joint_equal is calibration-feasible but the substantial reduction rule does not pass with adequate completion and precision
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.constrainingOrContradictory: joint_equal is not calibration-feasible without violating completion or native policy/target preservation, or a primary endpoint materially increases under feasible matching
primaryAnchorsAndOutcomeRule.individualRegimes: activation, displacement, target-range, and success interventions are reported regardless of joint feasibility, but an infeasible regime's aggregation endpoints are descriptive and cannot satisfy the supportive rule

validation: exact native-control replay against S03 for every holdout scenario
dynamic null count, value-stratum, mobility, length, and pairing preservation
claimBoundaries: Kinetic matching is an intervention on the clean-room simulator, not a biological mechanism measurement.
A swap gate changes which native actions execute and may alter path length even though the policy proposal is unchanged.

Failure to match Selection target range while completing is evidence of a structural feasibility constraint under this intervention class, not proof that no alternative redesigned policy could match it.
Value conditioning can remove the policy-value pathway and remains diagnostic.
S07 does not run identity controls or start S08.
